problem: Unified VLN+ObjNav work relies on architectural fusion, mixed-task training and large VL pretraining, and even object-centric topological maps ground language via explicit cross-modal supervision (CLIP/VLMs). It is unexamined whether independently trained vision and language encoders already share structure usable for navigation.
motivation: If the Platonic Representation Hypothesis holds, vision-only ObjNav, cross-modal ObjNav and VLN are just different goal interfaces over one semantic manifold, and paired cross-modal supervision would be partly redundant. A vision-built object-centric topological map is a discrete approximation of that manifold, so language goals could be grounded into it relationally without paired data.
key_idea: Build a segment-based topological map whose edge weights mix geometric and DINOv3 semantic (cosine) distances, and ground language goal categories to visual clusters by training-free blind matching (quadratic assignment on pairwise distance matrices) between DINOv3 and GTR-T5 embeddings.
insight: Injecting a small amount of self-supervised semantic distance into the graph improves navigation: on HM3D-IIN, lambda_s=0.2 gives SPL 62.6 vs 59.1 for pure geometry, while lambda_s=0.5 drops to 56.3, so too much semantics hurts. Non-trivial OVON performance without any paired vision-language data is offered as evidence that relational geometry is shared across encoders. Segmentation quality is a major bottleneck (FastSAM roughly halves SPL from 62.6 to 29.5).
method: Platonic Topological Map: nodes are object segments with DINOv3 embeddings (mean-pooled patch tokens in mask, L2-normalised); built on ObjectReact's topometric graph with intra-image geometric edges and cross-view association edges
Hybrid edge weight: d = λg·d_geo + λs·d̃_plat, where d_plat is cosine distance of embeddings, rescaled to metres via the 95th-percentile ratio with clipping at c=2.0; (λg,λs)=(0.8,0.2)
Cluster prototypes: K-means over node embeddings into K category-level clusters (K = closed vocabulary size) to bridge instance-vs-category granularity

Blind matching: solve the quadratic assignment min_π Σ(D^v_kl − D^l_π(k)π(l))² between visual centroid and GTR-T5 category-embedding distance matrices (factorized Hahn-Grant relaxation from 'It's a Match'), with no paired data

Goal localization and planning: candidate goal set = nodes of the matched cluster; Dijkstra under hybrid weights gives the min-cost goal; path costs are projected onto segmentation masks as a costmap for the frozen ObjectReact controller
Real-world deployment: Unitree Go2 Air, RGB-only teach-and-repeat, SAM2 segments, DINOv3 linear-probe background filtering, off-board laptop via ROS2

OVON and R2R-CE use unspecified 'short-horizon subsets', so they are not directly comparable to full-split baselines. No real-world quantitative results are given.
results: On HM3D-IIN PlatonicNav gets SPL 62.6 / SSPL 70.8 vs ObjectReact 59.1 / 64.6. On OVON val-unseen it reaches SR 48.7 / SPL 22.0, above MTU3D (40.8/12.1) and Uni-NaVid (39.5/19.8), though on a short-horizon subset. On R2R-CE it reports SR 63.5 / SPL 40.4, which has a high SR but a low SPL and trails CorrectNav (65.1/62.3) on SPL.
limitations: Bounded by segmentation quality, blind-matching robustness, language encoder expressiveness and the ObjectReact controller's long-range ability; long R2R-CE instructions remain challenging

OVON and R2R-CE evaluated on unspecified short-horizon subsets, so comparisons with full-split baselines are not like-for-like; IIN uses GT masks; the real-world evaluation is qualitative teach-and-repeat only
Blind matching needs a closed category vocabulary and K-means clustering; the evidence for the Platonic hypothesis is indirect (non-trivial performance and trajectory similarity)
